svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.20 MASONRY AND INSULATING CONCRETE FORM WALLS NOT IN CONTACT WITH THE GROUND
Mortar and Grout Mixes

g.text: Exterior, at or below ground: foundation

1 to 2 times the sum of the
Mortar used and placed within, Sentence (5)
Mortar and grout made off-site in a batching

Type S portland cement-lime where exposed to
the exterior, Type S or N where protected

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Mortar types are in accordance with Table 9.20.3.2.-A
(cells A to F).
Mortar for glass block masonry is (a) Type S portland
cement-lime where exposed to the exterior, or (b) Type S
or N where protected from the exterior.
Mortar is mixed within the proportion limits of Table
9.20.3.2.-B, with enough water for a consistency
adequate for laying masonry units.
Grout is mixed within the proportion limits of Table
9.20.3.2.-C, with enough water for a suitable flow to
fill all voids completely, without excessive segregation
or bleeding.
Except as in Sentence (6), mortar is used and placed in
final position
(a) within 1.5 h after mixing when the air temperature is
25°C (77°F) or higher, or (b) within 2.5 h after mixing when
it is less than 25°C.
Mortar and grout with a set-control admixture are made
off-site in a batching plant and placed within the
useful life stipulated by the manufacturer.
Grout used for reinforced masonry is placed to
CAN/CSA-A371, "Masonry Construction for Buildings."
Drawn: masonry cut through, one element per cell. Proportions are parts by volume as in the tables.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.20.3.2. (page 9-139)
